The CTA is conditional on a driver WITHOUT 'taxi' in service_types. Recommendation for next testing pass: use admin to first remove 'taxi' from a known driver (e.g. jean.dupont via PUT /api/admin/drivers/{id}/service-types with ["courier"]), log in via email/password as that driver, navigate to /chauffeur and confirm become-taxi-cta is visible; click it and confirm /chauffeur/profile?services=1 auto-opens driver-services-modal. critical_code_review_comments: BUG FOUND & FIXED in /app/backend/routes/misc.py PUT /admin/drivers/{driver_id}/service-types: find_one used positive projection {'_id':0,'taxi_mode':1} — when the driver document has NO taxi_mode field, MongoDB returns {} which is falsy in Python, causing the `if not driver` branch to wrongly return 404 even though the driver exists. Reproduced on jean.dupont (driver_b366adb552eb). FIX applied: changed projection to include 'id' and the truthiness check to `if driver is None`. This impacted any approved demo driver whose taxi_mode key was never written.

Endpoint correctly enforces admin permission drivers.approve, whitelists allowed values, sets taxi_mode='car' automatically when taxi is enabled and previous taxi_mode was None (override of VTC gate), and clears taxi_mode when taxi removed.

Frontend AdminDrivers.js exposes all required data-testids (drivers-table, services-cell-{i}, services-btn-{i}, driver-services-modal, admin-service-taxi/delivery/courier, admin-services-save). Modal closes on Save and the Services column reflects the new badges after save.

data-testid='driver-services-modal' is reused for both the admin modal (AdminDrivers.js) and the driver-side modal (DriverProfilePage.js). They live on different routes so there is no runtime conflict, but a test reading this testid from a wrong route would target the wrong dialog. Consider renaming the admin one to 'admin-driver-services-modal' for clarity.

rca of the issue: PUT /admin/drivers/{driver_id}/service-types returned 404 for drivers without taxi_mode key. Root cause: MongoDB projection {'_id':0,'taxi_mode':1} returns {} (empty dict) when the requested field is missing on the document; `if not driver` then treats {} as falsy. Fix: include 'id' in projection and change check to `if driver is None`. Mitigation deployed in /app/backend/routes/misc.py.
